overview.title: Fishing Port & Waterfront
overview.p1: Lively water edge, blue wooden boats, and great views of the Mazagan fortifications.
overview.p2: The golden hour light brings out the warm tones of the historic rampart stone.
overview.p3: Finish your walk here after visiting the cistern and ramparts for a final view of the Atlantic.

moods.title: What to see at the Port & Waterfront
moods.subtitle: Best experienced during golden hour when the fortifications catch the late sun.

1.title: Main Focus
1.desc: Working harbour edge, fishing boats, and warm evening glow on the walls.

2.title: Closer Look
2.desc: Watch fishermen mend nets and prepare traditional blue wooden boats.

3.title: Take Your Time
3.desc: Enjoy a relaxed stroll along the harbour promenade at sunset.

1.title: Best Timing
1.desc: Morning for the lively fish catch arrival, or late afternoon for sunset photography.

2.title: Footwear & Wind
2.desc: Docks can be damp — wear comfortable, sturdy shoes and bring a light windbreaker.

3.title: Combine nearby
3.desc: Pair your harbour visit with the ramparts, Portuguese City, and fresh seafood lunch.

food.title: Food nearby
food.p1: Fresh seafood stalls and oceanfront cafés just steps from the harbour docks.
food.p2: Enjoy grilled fish right by the water after exploring the boats.

q1.question: Is the port free to enter?
q1.answer: Yes, strolling along the harbour promenade and waterfront is free and open to everyone.

q2.question: How long should I spend here?
q2.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is ideal for walking around, taking photos, and watching the boats.

q3.question: Best time of day to visit?
q3.answer: Late afternoon and golden hour before sunset for the best light on the ramparts.

q4.question: What to combine it with?
q4.answer: Combine it with the Portuguese Cistern, ramparts, and a fresh seafood meal nearby.

q5.question: Is it family friendly?
q5.answer: Yes, it's a great spot for families to stroll and see local fishing boats up close.
